description:
Avantos was founded in New York in 2024 by Bassam Chaptini, a former McKinsey & Company partner, and Rabih Ramadi, previously Chief Revenue Officer at Unqork and Senior Partner and Head of Capital Markets at KPMG; the two serve as co-CEOs. In February 2026 the company announced a $25 million Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners with participation from strategic investors Vanguard and SEI, bringing total funding raised to $35 million. Business Wire headlined the announcement as "Avantos Raises $35 Million to Power the Future of Client Servicing in Financial Services", reflecting cumulative capital rather than the round size alone.
Avantos describes itself as an AI-native operating system for client management in financial services. It layers a knowledge graph on top of a firm's existing core systems to create a shared context layer that both humans and AI agents can act on, with agents covering client onboarding, ongoing servicing and growth workflows across wealth, protection and retirement businesses. The platform integrates with custodians, CRMs, portfolio management tools, underwriting systems and policy administration platforms rather than replacing them. Reported clients and design partners include Vanguard, Guardian Life, SEI and Mercer Advisors, and the company is SOC 2 certified.
The company sells to financial institutions as an enterprise software platform, and the Series A proceeds are earmarked for expanding its AI agent library and deepening integrations with custodial, CRM and policy administration systems. description:
The company was founded in 2023 as Greenlite AI by Will Lawrence (CEO, previously on Facebook's anti-money-laundering team) and Alex Jin, and went through Y Combinator in 2023. In May 2025 it raised a $15 million Series A led by Greylock with participation from Thomson Reuters Ventures, Canvas Prime and Y Combinator, bringing total funding to about $20 million. On 10 February 2026 the company announced a $75 million Series B and simultaneously rebranded from Greenlite AI to Bretton AI, positioning itself as "the AI standard for financial crime"; Fortune reported Sapphire and Greylock among the backers of that round.
Bretton AI provides an agentic AI platform that automates financial crime compliance operations for regulated banks, credit unions and fintechs. Its agents plug into a customer's existing compliance stack and handle anti-money laundering, know-your-customer and sanctions workflows — triaging alerts, executing first-line analyst tasks, and supporting onboarding, risk review and remediation. The company emphasises model validation and AI governance so that its output can withstand regulatory scrutiny, and says the Series B will fund expansion into additional financial crime domains and deeper regulatory engagement.
Bretton AI sells enterprise software to regulated financial institutions; press coverage frames the value proposition around cutting compliance operating costs and speeding customer onboarding. No published pricing tiers or contract structure were found on the fetched sources, so the revenue model was not verified beyond it being an enterprise B2B platform.

main_investors: Emergence Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Primary Venture Partners, SoFi
description:
Casap is a payment disputes automation and first-party fraud prevention platform co-founded and led by CEO Shanthi Shanmugam, who spent about six years at Robinhood as a group product manager for customer care before starting the company. In October 2024 Casap announced $8.5 million in seed funding to scale an AI-powered disputes and chargeback solution for banks, credit unions and fintechs. On 7 August 2025 the company announced a $25 million Series A led by Emergence Capital with participation from Lightspeed, Primary Ventures and SoFi, bringing total funding to $33.5 million — described by the company and by trade press as the largest venture investment to date in the issuer-side payment disputes space. Shanmugam was named to Inc.'s 2026 Female Founders 500 list and Casap was named AI Company of the Year by Tearsheet.
The product automates the full dispute lifecycle for financial institutions: AI agents analyse evidence, predict outcomes and automate intake through to chargeback filing, while a proprietary first-party fraud score — which the company likens to "FICO for first-party fraud" — flags suspicious behaviour before a refund is issued. Casap targets first-party fraud, which it cites as a roughly $100 billion problem accounting for 30–50% of all fraud losses. The company reports that customers cut fraud losses by more than half and scale dispute operations without adding headcount; published customer stories include Chartway (85% reduction in dispute costs) and MidSouth.
Casap sells to banks, credit unions and fintechs as an enterprise platform with built-in regulatory expertise and card-network integrations. No pricing page or published tiers were found, so the revenue model was not verified beyond being enterprise B2B software.

description:
FurtherAI was founded in 2023 by Aman Gour and Sashank Gondala and went through Y Combinator. The company raised a $5 million seed round backed by Nexus Venture Partners, Y Combinator and others, then announced a $25 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz in October 2025 — described by several trade outlets as one of the largest Series A rounds in insurance AI — bringing total funding to $30 million. Y Combinator's company page lists 36 employees based in San Francisco.
FurtherAI markets itself as "the AI workspace for insurance", built for MGAs, carriers, brokers and claims teams to automate complex workflows across the insurance value chain. Its AI workers handle repetitive, document-heavy tasks such as submission intake, quote generation, policy processing and claims work, addressing labour shortages in commercial insurance. The company says it processes billions in premiums for leading insurers, and one investor profile states customers write over $15 billion in premiums across all 50 US states. Series A proceeds are earmarked for expanding its library of insurance workflows, deepening integrations with carrier and broker systems, and growing the sales team.
FurtherAI sells enterprise software to insurance organisations. No published pricing tiers were found on the fetched sources, so the commercial model (subscription vs. per-workflow/usage pricing) was not verified.

description:
Questflow announced a $6.5 million seed round on 22 July 2025, led by CyberFund with participation from Delphi Labs, Systemic Ventures, Eden Block, White Star Capital, Web3.com, Animoca Brands, HashKey Capital, Wagmi Ventures, ElizaOS, the Tezos Foundation and CatcherVC, plus grants from ecosystem foundations including Aptos. In August 2026 the company announced a brand evolution repositioning itself as an "AI Finance Agent" platform focused on financial intelligence for retail and professional investors.
Questflow's original positioning was as the orchestration layer for the multi-agent economy. Its core technology, the Multi-Agent Orchestration Protocol (MAOP), lets AI agents communicate, coordinate and execute workflows directly on-chain in real time, removing silos between AI systems while keeping human review for sensitive decisions; the company frames agents as autonomous economic participants rather than assistants. After the 2026 repositioning, the platform turns professional investment strategies into transparent, configurable and executable AI Finance Agents, giving investors access to expert financial intelligence while retaining control of their capital.

main_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Matrix Partners, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Michael Ovitz
description:
Salient was founded in early 2023 by Ari Malik and Mukund Tibrewala and went through Y Combinator; the idea originated from Malik's experience with outdated, high-cost loan servicing systems while working at Tesla. In July 2025 the company raised a $60 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz with participation from Matrix Partners, Y Combinator and entrepreneur Michael Ovitz, reported at a $350 million valuation. By December 2025 Fortune reported Salient had reached roughly $25 million in annualised recurring revenue and a valuation of about $500 million. PitchBook lists total funding of $60.5 million.
Salient builds AI-native loan servicing for consumer and auto lenders. Its AI agents handle borrower interactions across voice, text, email and web chat — payment collection, due-date changes, extensions, payoffs, insurance updates and general queries — and the platform also covers collections, regulatory audit and dispute resolution, with compliance monitoring built in. The company says it has processed over $1 billion in transactions since launching in 2023 and reduces handle times by around 60%; named customers include Westlake Financial, Consumer Portfolio Services and American Credit Acceptance.
Salient sells enterprise software to lenders and financial services companies. No public pricing tiers were found on the fetched sources; the reported ARR indicates a recurring-revenue contract model, but the exact pricing structure was not verified.

description:
Tidalwave is led by co-founder and CEO Diane Yu and is headquartered at 25 W 39th Street, New York. On 14 November 2025 (announced publicly around 21 November 2025) the company disclosed a $22 million Series A led by Permanent Capital, with participation from D.R. Horton — the largest US homebuilder — and a follow-on from Engineering Capital, bringing total funding to $24 million. D.R. Horton became both an investor and an enterprise customer, planning to deploy the platform at its DHI Mortgage subsidiary; Mark Winter, CEO of DHI Mortgage, was quoted in the announcement.
Tidalwave builds agentic AI for mortgage origination — autonomous software agents that complete mortgage tasks end-to-end with minimal oversight. The platform connects directly to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac for instant underwriting decisions and integrates with Plaid, Argyle and Truv for real-time income, employment and asset verification, eliminating back-and-forth document collection. It provides real-time, multilingual borrower guidance, including tailored support for Spanish-speaking clients. Adopters include NEXA Lending, First Colony Mortgage and Mortgage Solutions, and the company says it is on track to power over 200,000 loans annually — roughly 4% of US mortgage originations forecast for 2025 by the Mortgage Bankers Association.
Tidalwave sells its agentic mortgage point-of-sale platform to lenders as enterprise software; it holds an AICPA SOC 2 attestation. No published pricing tiers were found on the fetched sources, so the revenue model was not verified.

founders: Gabriele Corso, Jeremy Wohlwend, Saro Passaro
description:
Boltz grew out of MIT CSAIL research associated with Regina Barzilay's group and a sequence of open model releases: Boltz-1 (November 2024), the first fully open-source model to approach AlphaFold 3 accuracy for biomolecular complex structure prediction; Boltz-1x; Boltz-2 (June 2025), released with Recursion, jointly modelling structure and binding affinity; and BoltzGen (October/November 2025), a generative protein binder design model. On 8 January 2026 the team formally launched Boltz PBC, a public benefit corporation led by Gabriele Corso as CEO alongside co-founders Jeremy Wohlwend and Saro Passaro, announcing a $28 million seed round with Zetta, Amplify and a16z named as leads plus Obvious Ventures, Factorial Capital and angels including Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue. The same day it announced a multi-year partnership with Pfizer.
Boltz builds open biomolecular AI models and packages them into products usable without specialist ML or infrastructure work. Its hosted platform, Boltz Lab (released in beta), combines the models with managed compute, scalable infrastructure and collaborative interfaces, plus two initial discovery agents: a small-molecule agent pairing an optimised Boltz-2 affinity predictor with a parallel SynFlowNet in an active-learning loop restricted to synthesisable Enamine REAL compounds, and a protein design agent building on BoltzGen with a new binding-confidence scoring head. The company says its models are used by more than 100,000 scientists across large pharmaceutical companies and thousands of biotechs, and it explicitly positions itself as a software and infrastructure provider rather than a therapeutics developer. Under the Pfizer partnership, Boltz refines its foundation models on Pfizer's historical data to create exclusive models, with Pfizer retaining ownership of compounds discovered using the platform.
Revenue comes from the hosted Boltz Lab platform and from enterprise partnerships such as the Pfizer collaboration. Boltz says model optimisation lets it offer generous free tiers and lower costs than running the open-source models yourself, and commits to three guarantees: users own what they build, customer data stays secure, and Boltz does not train on customer data. A pricing page exists at boltz.bio/pricing but its tiers were not retrieved, so specific price points were not verified.

main_investors: Fifty Years, Basis Set Ventures, Mythos Ventures, Footwork, Preston-Werner Ventures
description:
Elicit began as a project inside Ought, a non-profit machine learning research lab co-founded by Andreas Stuhlmüller and Jungwon Byun in 2018. In September 2023 Elicit spun out of Ought as an independent public benefit corporation alongside a $9 million seed round. In 2025 it raised a $22 million Series A — reported at a roughly $100 million valuation — with existing investors Fifty Years, Basis Set and Mythos participating alongside new backers including Footwork; Preston-Werner Ventures is also an investor. At the time of the Series A the company said Elicit was used by more than 400,000 researchers monthly; its site now states over 2 million researchers in academia and industry.
Elicit is an AI research assistant for evidence-based reasoning, aimed at systematic literature reviews and evidence synthesis. It searches across more than 138 million academic papers, produces one-sentence abstracts and summaries, extracts structured data from papers into tables, generates automated reports, identifies themes across studies, supports full-text chat with source citations, and imports from Zotero. Higher tiers add a dedicated systematic review workflow that screens thousands of papers, figure extraction, real-time collaboration, and admin usage tracking.
Elicit monetises through a published per-seat subscription. The Basic tier is free with limited Research Agent and Research Report usage but unlimited search, summaries and paper chat. Pro is $49 per user per month billed annually ($588/year) and adds a systematic review workflow screening 5,000 papers, 20 table columns at a time, extraction from up to 135 data sources, 10 research alerts, custom extractions and API access. Scale is $169 per user per month billed annually ($2,028/year) with 5x usage, figure extraction, live collaboration, up to 200 data sources, 30 columns and an admin panel. An Enterprise tier is custom-priced, adding screening of 40,000 papers, 40 columns, unlimited alerts and API access, SSO/SAML, 2FA, single-tenancy deployments, no training on customer data by default, and a dedicated customer success team.
confidence_notes: Founded year 2023 refers to the spin-out as an independent public benefit corporation; the underlying project started at Ought (founded 2018). Total funding of $31M is the sum of the $9M seed and $22M Series A. Oakland, California HQ comes from VCBacked, a secondary aggregator, not from Elicit's own site. Employee count not found. Series A investor list is partial (the fetched excerpt named Footwork and existing investors but the lead was not fully legible).

description:
Ellipsis Health was founded in 2017 by Mainul Mondal (Founder and CEO), Dr. Michael Aratow (co-founder and Chief Medical Officer) and Susan Solinsky. Mondal's motivation came from his childhood experience caring for his mother, who had severe depression, and the co-founders' observations in California safety-net hospitals that emotional health drives outcomes but is rarely measured objectively. The company raised $26 million in Series A funding announced in 2021, and later a $45 million Series A round; aggregator data reports roughly $75 million raised in total across three rounds.
Ellipsis Health's proprietary Empathy Engine is built on patented vocal biomarker technology, trained on millions of live clinical patient calls, and combines natural language processing with acoustic models spanning a range of age groups and cultural backgrounds. It analyses vocal biomarkers in a person's speech to identify, measure and monitor the severity of depression and anxiety — what the company describes as the first clinically validated speech-based mental health vital sign. The company has extended this into AI-powered voice agents for care management, sold to providers and payers to manage patients with complex physical, behavioural and social needs.

main_investors: Define Ventures, Flare Capital Partners, GV, MultiCare Capital Partners, Intermountain
description:
Layer Health is a Boston-based healthcare AI company founded by AI and clinical leaders from institutions including MIT, Harvard, Microsoft and Google; MIT professor David Sontag, Ph.D., is CEO and co-founder. On 27 March 2025 the company announced a $21 million Series A led by Define Ventures with participation from Flare Capital Partners, GV and MultiCare Capital Partners. In June 2025 Intermountain made a strategic investment in the company to improve chart review.
Layer Health's platform applies large language models trained on longitudinal patient data to automate medical chart review, interpreting both structured and unstructured clinical data at what the company describes as clinician-level accuracy. Rather than relying on predefined rules, its AI reasons like a clinician across a patient's whole chart to handle nuanced scenarios. Target use cases span quality reporting and clinical registries, clinical research and real-world data abstraction, hospital operations and revenue cycle management (clinical documentation integrity and coding), and clinical decision support. Reported results include reducing quality data abstraction time by more than 65% for the Froedtert & the Medical College of Wisconsin health network, and completing real-world data extraction for dozens of patients in a few hours in a collaboration with a leading cancer organisation — a process that had previously taken more than a year.
Layer Health sells to health systems, life sciences companies and research partners; its press release frames value in terms of reduced costs and "net-new" revenue opportunities for partners. No published pricing was found on the fetched sources, so the commercial model was not verified.

description:
Penguin Ai was founded in 2024 by Fawad Butt, who serves as CEO and co-founder. Butt previously held C-level roles at the largest US healthcare organisations, including Chief Data Officer at Kaiser Permanente, UnitedHealthcare and Optum, and spent time at Canvas Ventures evaluating healthcare investments. In September 2025 the company announced it had closed $29.7 million in venture funding, including a $25 million Series A led by Greycroft, with UPMC Enterprises and Snowflake Ventures also backing the company.
Penguin Ai offers a full-service generative AI platform built for health insurance payers, providers and hospital systems, aimed at what the company describes as healthcare's roughly $1 trillion-a-year administrative burden. The platform combines task-specific small language models, digital workers and agents to automate administrative workflows including prior authorisation, claims processing and adjudication, medical coding, risk adjustment, medical records summarisation and billing — delivering multiple payer and provider use cases on a single platform rather than as point solutions.
Penguin Ai sells enterprise software to payers, providers and revenue cycle management companies. No published pricing tiers were found on the fetched sources, so the revenue model was not verified.

description:
Periodic Labs was founded in 2025 by Liam Fedus, former VP of post-training research at OpenAI who announced his departure on 17 March 2025 to start an AI materials-science company, and Ekin Dogus Cubuk, a former Google Brain/DeepMind research scientist who led materials work there. The company emerged from stealth roughly six months later, in October 2025, with a $300 million seed round — one of the largest ever — backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Felicis, NVIDIA, Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt, DST Global and Lightspeed Venture Partners. By March 2026, press reports indicated the company was in deal talks at a valuation of around $7 billion.
Periodic Labs is building AI scientists and the autonomous physical laboratories for them to work in — "from bits to atoms". The aim is to generate genuinely new scientific knowledge by having AI systems design and run real physical experiments, produce high-quality experimental data and validate hypotheses against reality, combining robotics, machine learning and physics. The initial focus is materials discovery for sectors such as energy, electronics and infrastructure, including targets like superconductors.
The business model was not verified. The company is at a pre-commercial research stage and no pricing, licensing or partnership revenue structure was published on the fetched sources.

Qualified Health provides an enterprise AI platform for health systems, structured as a public benefit corporation. It gives health systems the infrastructure to deploy generative AI safely across both clinical care and administrative workflows, with end-to-end governance, measurable return on investment and centralised oversight of AI use. The company states its platform is trusted by 400,000 users.
Qualified Health sells enterprise platform contracts to health systems. No published pricing tiers were found on the fetched sources, so the revenue model was not verified.
